construction: the filemark after tape file 7 (B-C) is removed; after tape file 8's filemark, a foreign file of 2 records is appended, with its trailing filemark

scanner.reasoning: With BC and C joined, C's records lie at 28 + 2N .. 30 + 2N and their filemark at 31 + 2N; the appended file (2 records + filemark) puts the tape's EOD at 35 + 2N; every footer plans EOD at 33 + 2N. Spacing back: the record before the last filemark is foreign (magic miss); C's footer is read at 30 + 2N but records 31 + 2N, so no layout; B's footer is at its recorded position but its planned EOD is before the tape's EOD, so not used; AB's is a separation footer; A's footer, like B's, is not used. No footer supplies a layout, so no replica validates. (Without the appended file, B's layout would have been used and B and A accepted as a degraded inventory; the appended file is what removes that.)
scanner.then: Returns BotStructuralRecoveryRequired, performs the Section 8.4.1 walk, and reports that terminal authority was not recovered.
quotes: A terminal replica's footer that parses supplies a planned layout only when its recorded footer position equals the position at which it was read, and the layout's planned EOD is at or after the tape's EOD.
A layout whose planned EOD lies before the tape's EOD may be followed by later tape files, so it is not used, and when no footer supplies a layout, no replica validates;
A magic or CRC miss invalidates that candidate.
if no replica validates, perform the BOT structural recovery walk in Section 8.4.1.

If A, B, and C all fail, the Scanner returns an explicit `BotStructuralRecoveryRequired` outcome and performs the Section 8.4.1 walk; BOT Object classifications are likewise streamed before their terminal summary.
The walk does not invent a terminal replica. The Scanner MUST report that terminal authority was not recovered.

tape_files.1: Object candidate by elimination (item 7); identity unknown
tape_files.7: IndexSeparationExtent BC (item 3), damaged: measured N + 3 records against planned N (TerminalIndexSeparationParse); C is inside this file and is not seen as a tape file
tape_files.8: foreign file of 2 records: OPEN, see open_points

walk.ends: EOD at the start of tape file 9
walk.object_identities: tape file 1: unknown; tape file 8, if admitted as an Object candidate, also unknown
open_points: Tape file 8. The ladder (item 7) makes it an Object candidate by elimination; Section 12.6 forbids admitting 'a structural artifact after the exact terminal suffix' as an Object, but this suffix is not exact (BC's filemark is missing) and 'structural artifact' is undefined. Permitted: (a) Object candidate by elimination, identity unknown, first ordinal 4, outside the validated scope; (b) nonconformant trailing file, not admitted as an Object. Either way it is outside the validated scope and never a recovery input, and the validation of files 0..3 is unaffected.
quotes: matching separation-header magic commits the tape file to this control type under the same malformed-control and measured count rules.
Under items 2 and 3 the file keeps its control type, damaged; under items 4, 5 and 6, as under item 1, the file is not recognised, and item 7 applies.
Item 7 applies to a tape file that none of items 1 to 6 recognises.
A structural artifact after the exact terminal suffix is nonconformant and MUST NOT be admitted as an Object.
A normal finalized tape has the exact terminal suffix of Section 8.3 and EOD immediately after C's trailing filemark.

A map produced by the Section 8.4.1 walk, after the second pass of Section 12.3, is validated against the tape's final ParityMap when that ParityMap validates and is marked `is_final_directory`, and the map's canonical projection (Section 7.3) through the ParityMap's own entry hashes to its `canonical_map_digest`.
The validated scope and durable boundary are the first `directory_scope_tape_file_count` tape files, ending with that ParityMap's entry; `W` is `directory_scope_highest_protected_ordinal`.
MUST treat rows beyond the validated prefix as forensic only, never as recovery inputs.
